Cell boundary

Plasma membrane

A phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins forms a selective boundary. Channels, pumps and receptors regulate transport and communication.

How structure helps

The bilayer makes a boundary; its proteins make that boundary selectively permeable and responsive.

Structure 1 / 14

A typical nucleated animal cell, shown schematically. The cutaway exposes selected lumens; organelle sizes, counts, positions and transport timing are illustrative. The protein sequence simplifies intermediate compartments and recycling traffic. The RNA message and the newly made protein are different molecules.
